name: Primebook
tagline: Low-cost Android laptops for students, running its own PrimeOS
excerpt: Primebook, a Delhi startup making budget Android laptops for students, took a ₹75 lakh deal from Peyush Bansal and Aman Gupta on Shark Tank India Season 2.
content:
Primebook makes affordable laptops that run PrimeOS, its own Android-based operating system, aimed at students who cannot afford a conventional computer. The company was founded by IIT Delhi graduates Aman Verma and Chitranshu Mahant and is based in Delhi.

On Shark Tank India Season 2, Episode 11, the founders offered 1.5% of the company for ₹75 lakh. The pitch drew several offers, including individual bids and a combined offer from all five sharks on the panel. They accepted a joint offer from Peyush Bansal and Aman Gupta of ₹75 lakh for 3%, which Business Today reported as a ₹25 crore valuation.

After the show, Entrackr reported in April 2025 that Primebook raised $2 million in a pre-Series A round mixing equity and debt, from investors including Inflection Point Ventures and Auxano Capital. Revenue and a current valuation have not been reported in the outlets we track.

Primebook's pitch shows how a clear social goal, putting a laptop in every student's hands, can turn a hardware business into a bidding contest.

shark_tank.pitch_summary: Primebook pitched budget Android laptops for students and asked ₹75 lakh for 1.5%. After several competing offers, it took Peyush Bansal and Aman Gupta's ₹75 lakh for 3%.

faq.q: Did Primebook get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Yes. Peyush Bansal and Aman Gupta invested ₹75 lakh for 3% in Season 2, Episode 11.

faq.q: Has Primebook raised money since Shark Tank?
faq.a: Yes. Entrackr reported a $2 million pre-Series A round in April 2025.
It has not been publicly disclosed in the reports we track.
Aman Verma and Chitranshu Mahant, both IIT Delhi graduates.

lessons: Owning the operating system, not just the hardware, gave the pitch a defensible story.
Multiple offers gave the founders room to pick the sharks closest to their customers.
Hardware for price-sensitive buyers needs patient capital; the company raised a mix of debt and equity afterwards.
notes: Inc42 Datalabs lists a small Jan 2023 seed entry from Anupam Mittal, which conflicts with the on-air sharks; not used. Entrackr's later extension story mentions a $15M valuation for the 2025 round, but the main article does not state it; left out.
